findings.title: Member add/remove routes use :id, but controller requires :group_id
findings.body: The new routes in config/routes.rb (`delete "members"` and `put "members"` inside `resources :groups`) produce paths like `/admin/groups/:id/members`, so the group id arrives in `params[:id]`. However `add_members` (and `remove_member` at line 85) call `params.require(:group_id)`, which raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing` for real HTTP requests. The JS client calls `/admin/groups/<id>/members.json`, so adding or removing members will always return 400 and the feature is broken. The specs pass only because they invoke controller actions directly with `group_id`, bypassing routing. Use `params[:id]` or configure the route with `param: :group_id`.

findings.title: Public members endpoint uses :group_id although route param is :id
findings.body: `GET /groups/:id/members` (from `resources :groups do get 'members' end`) places the group identifier in `params[:id]`, but this action calls `find_group(:group_id)`, which does `params.require(:group_id)`. Real HTTP requests therefore fail with `ActionController::ParameterMissing`. The admin group page now depends on this endpoint through `Discourse.Group#findMembers` (`/groups/<name>/members.json`), so the admin member list will not load. The `show` action correctly uses `find_group(:id)`; this action should do the same, or the route should be changed accordingly.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` — for example 50 users with limit 50, or 100 with limit 50 — this reports one extra page. That makes `showingLast` false on the last real page, so the Next button can navigate to an empty page before becoming disabled. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the existing zero-user guard).

findings.title: create ignores alias_level sent by the client
findings.body: The admin group form renders the alias level selector even for a new group, and the client sends `alias_level` in `asJSON()`. However `create` only sets `name` and `visible`; it never assigns `group.alias_level` from `params[:alias_level]`. The group is saved with the default alias level instead of the value the admin selected. The client model also only updates `id` after creation, so the UI may continue showing the selected value until a full reload, hiding the mismatch.

findings.title: Usernames are not stripped when splitting comma-separated input
findings.body: `add_members` does `usernames.split(",").each` and looks up each entry with `User.find_by_username`. If the input is `"alice, bob"`, the second entry is `" bob"` and lookup fails, so that member is silently not added even though the request still reports success. The username list should be split on commas and each token stripped before lookup.

findings.title: remove_member auto-group spec uses PUT for a DELETE action
findings.body: This test invokes `xhr :put, :remove_member` directly on the controller, but the actual route is `DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members`. Because controller specs bypass routing, this also fails to detect that real requests send `params[:id]` while the controller requires `:group_id`. The spec should use `xhr :delete, ...` and ideally an integration/request spec should exercise the routes, otherwise the broken endpoint passes tests.
